Vimuktātman
(A. D. 1200)
------------------------------------------
Vimuktātman is one of the important advaitins of the post-शङ्कर period. His famous work, the Iṣṭasiddhi, is widely acclaimed as a standard treatise, one of the four Siddhi-works, the other three being Advaitasiddhi, Brahmasiddhi and Naiṣkarmyasiddhi.
Except that he was a disciple of Avyayātman, nothing more is known about him.
He is said to have written one more work called Pramāṇa-वृत्ति-nirṇaya, not yet published.
See IṢṬASIDDHI also.

vimāna
(‘an object that is measured’)
------------------------------------------
Though etymologically this word is defined as something which is measured (mā = to measure), it is used in a technical sense. According to the works on ancient Hindu architecture it can mean any of the following: a chariot of the gods flying in heavenly regions; a होउसे or a palace, especially the one which is seven-storeys in height; the small tower over the गर्भगृह or the sanctum sanctorum of a temple.
This last one can be of three architectural types: नागर (curvilinear); द्राविड (pyramidal); वेसर (combination of the former two).
See also HINDU TEMPLES.
